title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a working page from the notes for the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex. Grothendieck has been analysing a structured bigraded object K^{··} over a space or topos X. From the previous pages, this is presumably a bigraded commutative differential algebra, possibly with divided powers, generated in low degrees. The page reads as the conclusion of a classification argument: such an object is determined by, and equivalent to, linear-algebra data in its generating degrees.

The data are:
(α) a commutative sheaf of rings k on X;
(β) a flat k-Module L, in the cases of interest invertible or even free of rank 1;
(γ) a k-Module Φ together with a monomorphism u: L → Φ. This is presumably the generating degree-one piece and the differential, or an inclusion of generators.

Grothendieck then describes morphisms. Let K'^{··} be given by (k', L', Φ', u'). A morphism K^{··} → K'^{··} compatible with all structures is equivalent to:
- a ring homomorphism λ_0: k → k';
- a λ_0-semilinear map λ_Φ: Φ → Φ' with λ_Φ(u(L)) ⊂ u'(L').
Such a λ_Φ then induces a λ_0-semilinear map λ_L: L → L'.

In modern terms, the category of such K^{··} is equivalent to a fibred category over rings. Its objects are pairs (Φ, a sub-k-module L ≅ flat or invertible) and its morphisms are semilinear maps preserving the submodule.

The last lines treat the special case where trivialisations L ≅ k and L' ≅ k' are given. Then one can forget L and regard Φ as a module with a marked section e = u(1). The condition on λ_Φ (cut off at the bottom of the page) should be λ_Φ(e) ∈ k'·e', i.e. λ_Φ(e) = c·e' for some c ∈ k', with c determined by λ_L(1).

The purpose is to set up the universal or classifying description of the PD de Rham-type complexes, so that functoriality, e.g. under Frobenius or base change, becomes simple linear algebra.
errors: No mathematical errors are visible. The statement is a sketch: the exact definition of K^{··} and the proof of the equivalence are on other pages.

The final condition is cut off. With marked sections, λ_Φ(e) should land in k'·e'. If one wants an isomorphism-type compatibility one would need the scalar to be a unit, but nothing on the page requires that.

ideas.what: Equivalence between structured bigraded (PD/dg) algebras K^{··} and linear data (k, flat/invertible L, monomorphism L → Φ)
ideas.modern_name: Free / universal objects determined by their generating data; classification of DG algebras generated in low degree (cf. PD-Koszul/de Rham complexes of a module)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in crystalline cohomology (Berthelot, Illusie's complexe cotangent et déformations, Berthelot–Ogus)
ideas.where_published: Not in his published texts as far as known; the IHÉS 1976 talk was not published

ideas.what: Morphisms as λ_0-semilinear maps Φ → Φ' preserving the line L, inducing λ_L
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms in a fibred category of 'modules with a sub-line' over the category of rings (semilinear maps)

ideas.what: When L ≅ k, replace (L ⊂ Φ) by Φ with a marked section
ideas.modern_name: Pointed modules / modules with a marked vector

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping reduction of a structured complex to linear-algebra data, with semilinear morphisms. It is useful inside the notes but contains nothing that would be new to a specialist in crystalline or PD de Rham theory.
transcription_corrections: 'k-schéma Φ' should almost certainly read 'k-Module Φ'. The data in γ) are an immersion of the k-Module L into a k-Module Φ.
'voire le livre' should read 'voire libre' (i.e. 'flat, or even invertible, or even free [of rank 1]...').
'Soit de = K'^{··}' should read 'Soit de même K'^{··} défini par (k', L', Φ', u')'.
The struck-out heading 'Soient K^{··} et K'' is correctly flagged; the beginning is illegible.
'Anneau commutatif[?]' is plausible (written 'Anneau comm...'), so 'k, Anneau commutatif sur X'.
Near the bottom the struck passage contains a draft 'L →λ L' / Φ → Φ'' diagram, followed by the clean 'L →λ_L L''.
